ordinary_alignment: Both refer to November 2026 seasonally adjusted BLS U-3. Polymarket YES is <=3.8%; Kalshi YES is >3.8%.
material_difference: Polymarket uses the last available month if specified data is unavailable by the following scheduled monthly release. Kalshi linked terms wait until a later expiration, up to three months after the original release, with an earlier expiration if the data arrives or is cancelled.
additional_uncertainty: Polymarket excludes revisions after the first release; Kalshi terms exclude revisions after Expiration. Their revision windows are not presumed equivalent.

hypothetical_counterexample.conditions: November data arrives after the following scheduled release but before Kalshi final expiration; no announcement that the data will never be released. Last available month is 3.8%; eventual November print is 4.0%.
hypothetical_counterexample.conclusion: An inverted normal-release mapping does not ensure $1 payout for both packages during this allowed delay scenario.
